THE DERIVATION MUST FAIL CLOSED ON A SHALLOW REPOSITORY, NOT DERIVE 154 WRONG KEYS SILENTLY. `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returns `true` in the shallow clone and `false` in the full one, measured, and the module already owns the correct behaviour for an artifact it cannot key: report it DEFERRED by name and append nothing. Deriving from a grafted history instead produces events whose `commit` field is a false statement about when a verdict entered the repository.

N2 FOUR CONCURRENT RECONCILIATIONS DUPLICATE EVERY EVENT, WITH NO LOCK AND NOTHING TO NOTICE. Over a 60-verdict fixture I ran four `reconcile-verdicts` processes at once: each reported `0 already recorded, 60 appended` and the log ended with 240 verdict events over 60 artifacts, 180 duplicates. No line was torn (each event is a single sub-4096-byte write to a file opened in append mode, so the writes are atomic in practice, and 0 of 240 lines failed to parse) and `validate.py events` exited 0. The next serial run then reported `60 already recorded, 0 appended`, so the duplicates are permanent in an append-only log. Read-then-append with no exclusion is the pre-existing house style, since verify.sh:132 appends its own gate event the same way, but the pre-existing appends were unconditional and claimed nothing, where AC2 claims exactly-once and names `a duplicate key in the log` as its refutation. The reachable shapes are two gate runs in one working tree at once, which is ordinary when a person and an agent both build, and CI matrix jobs sharing a checkout. Not blocking on its own; it is the same class as the clone-depth finding, which is that the log has no reader-side dedup to fall back on.

N3 A VERDICT INTRODUCED ONLY BY A MERGE COMMIT IS REPORTED WITH A FALSE MESSAGE AND NEVER GETS AN EVENT. Built it: a merge whose resolution adds proof/WARP-8002/verdict.json, present in NEITHER parent. `git log --diff-filter=A` does not diff merges, so the add map misses it and the run prints `1 deferred until committed (proof/WARP-8002/verdict.json)`. IT IS COMMITTED. The message is wrong about the only fact it states, and the artifact is deferred forever rather than for a moment. The manifest declares the mechanism honestly at assumptions (3) and this repository has exactly ONE merge commit in its whole history, so the surface is empty here; the shipped SENTENCE is still false and is one word from being right. A `--no-ff` merge whose add sits on the side branch resolves correctly, which I also checked.

N4 THE HOSTILE-INPUT SURFACE IS FAIL-OPEN ON THE PAYLOAD, WHICH IS DEFENSIBLE AND UNDECLARED. Over a fixture holding seven deliberately broken verdicts (not JSON at all, no `verdict` field, a value outside the vocabulary, an embedded newline plus a non-integer round, non-ASCII content, a bare `[]`, a bare `null`) the reconciler appended all seven and `validate.py events` exited 0 on the result. THE ENVELOPE IS NEVER MALFORMED, which is the property AC1 actually claims and it holds: the type is always the declared one, json.dumps escapes the embedded newline so no line can be split, and a `round` that is not an int is omitted rather than invented. But `verdict` is copied through unvalidated, so `TOTALLY-BOGUS-VALUE` lands in the log and would appear in metrics' verdict tally, where validate.py polices VERDICTS on the ARTIFACT and nothing polices it on the EVENT. The projection is the natural place to refuse a value the vocabulary does not know, or to omit it as it already omits a bad round. Also checked and clean: a 200-character spec directory, a directory name containing a space, and a non-ASCII directory name all key and validate correctly. A ROOT commit carrying a verdict resolves correctly. Two verdicts in one commit, and two for the SAME spec in one commit, get distinct keys and distinct ids.

And `passed` is the wrong token for a criterion whose letter is unmet: an automated reader of `every acceptance criterion is passed` will read it as satisfied, and the builder's argument against inventing an eleventh status is right without being the answer, because the answer was to AMEND AC3 IN THE SPEC BEFORE THE BUILD. residual_rulings.DOES THE KEY SURVIVE MERGE, RENAME AND R: MERGE YES, RE-ADD YES BY DESIGN, RENAME NO, AND CLONE DEPTH NO. A `--no-ff` merge whose add lives on the side branch resolves correctly. A verdict introduced ONLY by a merge resolution is missed and reported deferred with a false message (N3), declared in the assumptions, and this repository has one merge commit. DELETE THEN RE-ADD is stable and keeps the FIRST add, which is the documented choice: I re-added with a DIFFERENT result and the log kept the original, appending nothing. AMEND IN PLACE is the same mechanism and is NOT harmless, because this repository reuses verdict.json across rounds: it is how proof/WARP-1208/verdict.json came to be recorded as a fail, and it appends no second event, keeps the stale one, and does not crash. RENAME BREAKS IT: `--no-renames` sees the destination as a new add, so a renamed verdict gets a SECOND event for a review already recorded, one artifact in the corpus has already taken a rename commit's date as its `at`, and on the repository's own round-2 convention the projection can record the same round twice and the newer round not at all. ROOT COMMIT works. TWO ADDS IN ONE COMMIT work, including two for one spec, with distinct keys and distinct ids. SHALLOW CLONE is the sharpest failure: identical HEAD, 154 of 154 keys different at depth 1 and 135 of 154 at depth 50, silently, with a `commit` field that misstates history. `--filter=blob:none` and `--single-branch` are clean.

residual_rulings.CAN THE STAGE FAIL THE GATE, AND IS A ST: IT CANNOT, AND I COULD NOT MAKE IT, AND THE DESIGN CHOICE IS RIGHT. Five constructions, each exit 0 with a named reason on stdout: a read-only .warp with a read-only log (`not reconciled (PermissionError: ...)`), a log path that is a DIRECTORY (`not reconciled (IsADirectoryError: ...)`), a directory that is not a git repository (`0 verdict artifact(s) tracked`), an existing log holding a torn line and raw binary bytes (appends, keeps the garbage, exits 0), and git REMOVED FROM PATH (`0 tracked`, exit 0). Structurally the stage block is byte-identical in all eight gate scripts, mentions FAIL nowhere and guards the call with `||`. THE REASONING HOLDS: the log is append-only and the backfill is one-time, so a stage that reddened on a missing event would have made the very commit that introduces it unlandable, and bookkeeping should never be a verdict on a build. BUT THE FLIP SIDE IS REAL AND THIS REVIEW IS THE PROOF OF IT: a silently broken projection IS invisible. `validate.py events` exited 0 on a log with 154 duplicated events, and on a log carrying `verdict: TOTALLY-BOGUS-VALUE`, and on the shipped log whose WARP-1208 line contradicts its own artifact. Never failing the gate is right; publishing NO integrity signal at all is the gap. The honest form is a stage that still cannot redden but REPORTS what it found, which it already does for `deferred`, extended to the cases it currently cannot see: a shallow repository, a duplicate key, a path whose tracked content differs from what was recorded. All three are one line of report each and none of them touches FAIL.
residual_rulings.WHAT THIS ITEM GOT RIGHT: THE DESIGN, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A FIRST-ROUND FAIL ON A KEY AND NOT A REJECTION OF THE APPROACH. Making the event a PROJECTION of a committed artifact rather than an act someone remembers is correct, and putting the call in the always-run built-in section instead of the declarable catalog is the whole point rather than a detail; I verified it is in all eight scripts and is reachable by no `na:` or `waived:`. The domain is derived from `git ls-files` with no count anywhere in the module. Idempotence, append-only and the mtime independence are all real and all measured, and the two-clone proof reproduces the builder's published digests byte for byte, which is more than most records survive. The staged-not-committed deferral is exactly the right instinct: an artifact that cannot be keyed durably gets NAMED and skipped rather than keyed on a guess. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE SAME INSTINCT WAS NOT APPLIED TWICE MORE. A shallow repository cannot be keyed durably either, and a path whose content has been overwritten is not the artifact that was reviewed. The fix is one property, not a redesign: key the event to the REVIEW, for which the artifact's own blob sha is available from the same git pass, identical in every clone at every depth, changing when the artifact changes and not changing under a rename.

disposition: DO NOT LAND IT YET. THE DESIGN IS RIGHT AND ONE PROPERTY IS WRONG. Deriving the event from the committed artifact by code the gate always runs, instead of asking a reviewer to remember, is the correct answer to the failure this item exists to fix, and almost everything built around it holds under attack: the domain is genuinely derived with no count in the module, the stage is unskippable in all eight gate scripts, it cannot redden the build and I could not make it, it is idempotent and append-only and cheap, and its two-clone mtime proof reproduces the published digests byte for byte. WHAT IS WRONG IS THE KEY, AND IT IS WRONG IN THE ONE DIRECTION AN APPEND-ONLY LOG CANNOT SURVIVE. The key identifies a PATH'S FIRST APPEARANCE rather than a review, and this repository's own verdict convention both overwrites verdict.json across rounds and renames the previous round out to a new name. So the shipped 154 already contain a line asserting that proof/WARP-1208/verdict.json FAILED when the committed artifact says pass_with_notes round 2, which makes the item's single published benefit number wrong: {pass_with_notes 102, pass 38, fail 14} over the artifacts against the {pass_with_notes 101, pass 38, fail 15} in the manifest, the commit message and the log. On a fixture reproducing the same convention the projection records one round twice and the next round not at all. And the key is not stable across clones of one commit, which is the refutation AC2 wrote down for itself: `git clone --depth 1` at the same commit derives 154 of 154 different keys silently, doubling the tally, with a `commit` field that misstates history, on the default checkout of the most common CI. Both come from the same missing property and both are closed by the same one, since the artifact's own blob sha is available from the same git pass, is identical at every clone depth, changes when the artifact changes and does not move under a rename. THE THIRD THING I FOUND IS THE SENTENCE THAT LET THE FIRST TWO THROUGH. `Nothing reads these events yet` appears in the spec's Out of scope, in the manifest's assumptions and in the rollback, and it is false three times over: metrics.py reads them, the manifest measures its own headline with it, and runstatus.py renders them into a `recent verdicts` list that now shows 3 of the true 10 and omits the five newest verdicts in the repository. This repository's own rule is that an overstated sentence is deleted, not qualified. AC3 IS NOT WHY THIS FAILS. Its letter is genuinely unreachable, I verified the binding that makes it so rather than taking it on trust, the ten-entry list is exhaustive in both directions, and nothing was split or obfuscated to dodge a match: what shipped is stronger than what was asked. Its DISPOSITION is still the wrong record, and the fix is to amend the criterion in a spec this build was already correcting three other declarations in. THE FLOOR IS CLEAN ON EVERY ITEM AND THIS FAIL RESTS ON NONE OF IT: gate GREEN 3220 / 0 at 3:10.04 on my own clock, canon byte-identical across all 8 and all 7, RULE #1 clean over 2509 added lines, nothing pushed, and `git worktree list` ending at exactly three.
